judgment.notes: M001 is used with A=R, B=K via the unital map ρ proved in S001, T=M_R and the R-basis (b e_i) supplied by N003. D008 supplies the module; R is commutative and K a field, so all semiring/algebra premises hold. Its left-oriented tensors are converted by the explicitly balanced flip. M007 is used with q=p and natural d=r; H001 gives primality and r≤λ<p, excluding p≤r. Thus its equivalence gives p∤r!, including r=0. BG001 supplies only routine prime-residue-field background for S001, not a new tensor/localization input. No E applications occur.

S001 correctly derives the integer kernel from characteristic, keeps all denominators nonzero, and uses cross multiplication to define ρ; its zero criterion gives kernel pR. Reduction modulo p is surjective (integer representatives) and has that same kernel, giving the claimed residue identification; BG001 checks the prime-field property. H004 and h=xy−yx give the lattice actions. In S002 the two tensor isomorphisms have explicit balanced maps and inverses. The quotient inverse is representative-independent since p acts as zero on K; the composites fix generators. S003 applies the given basis-extension result, flips tensors, and transports the basis. Basis coordinates also verify the quotient basis assertion. Complex linearity transfers the N001 formulas to b e_i, and the explicit tensor maps transfer them to β. N002's endomorphisms act on M_R and hence on its scalar extension; their basis values identify them with ε and preserve the stated products. S004 inverts only nonzero factorials or images of R-units, then expresses each ε as a scalar times a composition of powers of x,y. Subspace stability under these operations follows directly by iterating invariance and scalar closure. Every index in that formula is in [0,λ]; λ=0 causes no exception.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
